1.why: All screens use a clean sans-serif typeface with adequate letter and line spacing, though spacing is ordinary rather than notably generous.

2.why: Instructional text is sentence case with no italics or dense blocks, though the 'STEP 1 OF 3' labels and 'NORTHSTAR BANK' brand use letter-spaced capitals.

3.why: Content is presented in a narrow single-column card with large text and buttons that would read well at mobile width, though the screenshots themselves are taken at a desktop viewport.

4.why: Each screen carries only one or two short plain-language sentences, e.g. 'Enter the six-digit code sent to your phone. The code expires in 10 minutes.'

5.why: Only the phone field shows an example placeholder ('+447700900000'); the email and verification code fields provide no example of expected input.

6.why: No long blocks of text appear on any screen; the longest text is a one-line test-mode log note that is not required reading.

7.why: No copy functionality is visible anywhere; the six-digit code must be typed by hand and no screens showing secrets or backup codes with copy options are provided.

8.why: No QR code or equivalent alternative to manual entry appears in any of the provided screenshots.

9.why: The fields are standard labelled inputs, but the screenshots provide no evidence to confirm or deny browser autofill or password manager support.

10.why: A 'Step X of 3' indicator and a large high-contrast primary button are present on every screen, though the step label is small.

11.why: Each screen asks for one main action via a single primary button ('Continue', 'Verify and continue'); 'Use different details' is clearly a secondary link.

12.why: Step transitions imply progress and the error banner says 'Please try again', but 'We could not complete that request' is vague about what happened and there is no explicit confirmation such as 'code sent'.

13.why: Retrying after the error is possible with the entered code retained, but no resend/re-request code option and no reveal/hide toggle is visible.

14.why: The error message 'We could not complete that request. Please try again.' is non-blaming and suggests a fix, but it does not state what the actual problem was.

15.why: No time limit is imposed on reading, and the code's 10-minute expiry is reasonably generous for entering a six-digit code, though a time limit does exist.
